(By Sri.K.R.Manjunatha, Advocate)
 Scch-24 2 Mvc 2921/2024
 Judgment
This claim petition is filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of Indian Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation for the injuries sustained by her in a road traffic accident.

2. The case of the petitioner is as follows:-
That on 17-03-2024 at 9.00 a.m., the petitioner was waiting for the bus along with her husband at Chagalahatti bus stop, Yelahanka Taluk, Bangaloreat that time the driver of the BMTC bus bearing Reg.No.KA-57-F-3368 came in a rash and negligent Jayamma vs B.M.T.C on 4 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/34857412/
1 manner and dashed to the petitioner and her husband, result of which she and her husband fell down and sustained injuries.
Immediately the petitioner was shifted to Regal Hospital, wherein she took treatment as an inpatient..

So far, the petitioner has spent Rs.1,50,000/- towards medical treatment, conveyance, attendant charges,
transportation charges.
3. Prior to the accident, the petitioner was hale and healthy.
She was doing flower business and earning Rs.700/- per day.
Due to the permanent disability, petitioner is not in a position to do the said work.
She has suffered pain and sufferings, permanent disability, loss of income, loss of future income and other pecuniary and non-pecuniary damages.

4. Respondent- the RC owner of BMTC Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-57-F-3368 has filed written statement and contended that the driver of the bus was proceeding from Bangaluru to Kempegowda bus station at about 9-10 to 09-20 am., and when the bus reached near Chagalahatty Bus stop, the petitioner all of a sudden stepped in to the road from the footpath without noticing the BMTC bus in order to cross the road and fell down on the road result of which she sustained injuries.
The driver of the bus had shown sympathy towards the pedestrians in getting them admitted to the Regal Hospital, wherein first aid treatment was given.
5. The respondent Corporation had paid interim compensation of Rs.10,000/- each on 17-03-2024 to the petitioner and her husband Chikkanna.
The said amount is liable to be deducted out of the award amount in case award is passed against the respondent.
Thus respondent prayed to dismiss the petition.

6. On the basis of the above pleadings the following issues are framed:
ISSUES 1.

Whether the Petitioner proves that on 17-03-2024 at about 9-00 a.m, when she was waiting for the Bus at Chagalahatti Bus stop, at that time, all of sudden the driver of BMTC Bus bearing registration No.KA-57-F-3368 drove the same at high speed, in a rash or negligent manner and dashed against her.
As a result of forced impact, the Petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries?
2. Whether petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, what is the quantum?
from whom?
(3) What order or award?
7. In order to prove the issues, petitioner got examined herself as P.W.1 and one witness is examined as PW.2 and got marked documents at Ex.P1 to Ex.P17.
The driver of the BMTC bus got examined as R.W.1 and got marked documents at Ex.R1 and R2.

Jayamma vs B.M.T.C on 4 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/34857412/
2 8.
Heard arguments of learned counsel for the petitioner and respondent and perused the entire materials placed on record.

9. My findings on the above issues are as follows:
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative Issue No.2: Partly in the affirmative.

Issue No.3: As per final order, for the following;
REASONS 10. Issue No.1:-

In order to explain the actionable negligence of the driver of offending vehicle, PW1 has filed her affidavit explaining the vivid picture of the accident that took place on on 17-03-2024 at 9.00 a.m., when the petitioner was waiting for the bus along with her husband at Chagalahatti bus stop, Yelahanka Taluk, Bangaloreat that time the driver of BMTC bus bearing Reg.No.KA-57-F-3368 (hereinafter referred to as the offending vehicle) came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the petitioner and her husband, result of which she and her husband fell down and sustained injuries.

P.W.1 further deposed about the nature of injuries sustained, treatment taken and the amount spent for treatment etc.
11.

In support of the claim and to prove the rash and negligent driving, the P.W.1 has relied upon Ex.P1 to Ex.P6, which are the police records such as F.I.R., Complaint, Spot sketch, Inspection report, Charge sheet, Wound certificate, etc.
12.

On the basis of the complaint lodged by Munikrishna, who is the brother of the petitioner, case has been registered against the driver of offending vehicle in Crime No.69/2024 of Devanahalli Traffic Police Station for the offence punishable under section 279 and 337 of IPC.
The investigation officer after investigation filed charge sheet against the driver of offending vehicle for the offence punishable under Section 279, 337 and 338 of IPC.

13. The learned counsel for respondent has vehemently submitted that the petitioner while crossing the road without observing the vehicular movement has come in contact with the offending vehicle,
hence petitioner too has contributed negligence.
On the point of contributory negligence, the learned counsel has relied upon following judgment.
14. In MFA No. 6024/2014 c/w MFA No. 13/2016 between Bangalore Metropolitan Transport Corporation Vs. Smt. Umadevi & Ors.,.

entities.text: Bangalore Metropolitan Transport Corporation Vs. Smt. Umadevi & Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Hon'ble High Court has assessed the contributory negligence on the part of the deceased at 10 % and on the offending vehicle at 90%.

In the said case,
the spot mahazar clearly demonstrated that there was no bus stop at the place of accident and the accident in question has taken place in the middle portion of the curved road where the deceased was not suppose to stand.
Hence, 10% of negligence is apportioned on the part of the deceased.

Jayamma vs B.M.T.C on 4 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/34857412/
3 15.

In MFA NO. 9345/2011 between Sri B Nagaraj Vs. The Managing Direction, BMTC & Anr., The Hon'ble High Court has set aside the order of the Tribunal which apportioned contributory negligence on the part of the claimant at 10%, by holding that at the time of accident the claimant already crossed 90% of the road and he was close to the footpath of the other side and the bus was proceeding towards bus stand and accident has taken place at a turn.

entities.text: Sri B Nagaraj Vs. The Managing Direction, BMTC & Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It was observed by the Hon'ble High Court that if the driver of the bus had driven it slowly he could have avoided the accident.

It is further observed that if there was provision for pedestrian to cross near by the place of accident and claimant crossed the road elsewhere, then there is justification to apportion the negligence even on the part of the claimant, but no material produced by the Insurer of the bus showing that there was provision for pedestrian crossing at the spot of accident or nearby.
16.

In the light of the observation made in the aforesaid judgment, if the averments of the written statement and line of cross examination done to the PW.1 is perused, the respondent has taken contradictory defence so far as the manner of accident is concerned.

At one breath they contend that the accident in question occurred while the petitioner was crossing the road and at another breath contends that the petitioner while trying to board the moving bus fell on the road and sustained injuries.
Hence, the respondent are not definite as to the manner in which in accident question has occurred whether while crossing the road unmindfully or whether while boarding the moving bus.

17. It is bent upon contended by the petitioner that at the time of accident, herself and her husband were proceeding at the edge of the road, at that time the offending vehicle came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against them result of which both of them sustained grievous injuries.
It is relevant to state here that at the time of accident along with the petitioner her husband was present and he too had sustained injuries as the impact of accident.

When it is the defence of the respondent at one breath that the petitioner while trying to board the moving bus has fell down and sustained injury, then it is for the respondent to state how could the husband of the petitioner who was with the petitioner has sustained injuries, because both the petitioner and her husband cannot try to board the moving bus at a time.

If the spot mahazar and sketch is perused, it is clearly stated that at the time of accident the petitioner and her husband as pedestrian were walking on the left side of the footpath and at that time the offending vehicle came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against them.
In the mahazar the spot of accident is shown as in the footpath road.
The spot sketch reveals that the spot of accident is on the extreme left side of the road.
It is one way road from Bagalur to Hennur and the road is sufficiently wide.
The offending vehicle is a heavy vehicle.

When road is sufficiently wide, the driver of the offending vehicle could have drive his vehicle in the middle of the road and there was no necessity for him to drive the vehicle on the extreme left side of the road touching to the footpath.

18. So far as the citation relied by the respondent is concerned, the observation made in the second citation goes against to the case of the respondent as the Hon'ble High Court had set aside the order of the Tribunal apportioning contributory negligence of 10% on the part of the claimant.
So far as the observation made in the first citation is concerned, in the said case accident has occurred in the middle of the curve road where the deceased was not suppose to stand.
But in the present case, the petitioner was standing by the edge of the road and there was no necessity for the offending vehicle to move the vehicle on the edge of the road touching to the footpath.

Jayamma vs B.M.T.C on 4 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/34857412/
4 19.
The Learned counsel for respondent has further relied upon the judgment reported in 1994 ACJ 1303 and 1994 ACJ 1303 (High Court Cuttak)
In the said two cases, it was observed that the contents of charge sheet cannot be treated as an evidence in a claim proceeding, Tribunal must rely upon the evidence led before it.

20. In the light of the observation made in the aforesaid judgment, by excluding the charge sheet, if the materials placed on record is carefully perused, it makes it clear that the driver of the offending vehicle has solely contributed negligence.
Hence, issue no.1 is answered in the affirmative.
21. Issue No.2:- P.W.1 has given evidence to the effect of her sustained severe injuries.
The petitioner has produced wound certificate and discharge summary which are marked as Ex.P6 and P7.
On going through the medical documents, it reveals that petitioner has taken treatment as inpatient from 17-03-2024 to 20-03- 2024 at Regal Hospital for a period of 4 days.
As per the wound certificate, the petitioner has sustained three injuries which are simple injuries in nature.

22. Dr.Shailesh A V Rao -Senior Consultant Neurosurgeon at Padmashree Diagnostics, Bengaluru is examined as PW.2 and through him OPD records, CT brain report, Neuro psychological assessment report, Mini mental state examination report are marked as Ex.P13 to P17.
P.W.2 has deposed that the petitioner consulted him at Padmashree Diagnostics, Bangalore on 20-06-2025 and again on 26-06-2025 for the assessment of his disability.
23. PW.2 further deposed that neuro psychological assessment of the petitioner was done on 23-06-2025.
Her IQ was of 86 (normal range 90-110).
She is below average in thinking and reasoning.
On IDEAS, she obtained a score of 06, suggestive of 40% mild disability.
PW.2 further deposed that MMSE was done to the petitioner on 26-06-2025, she obtained a low score of 18/30.
Pw.2 further deposed that the petitioner has neuro disability pertaining to cognition and that the petitioner has suffered permanent disability on whole body at 10%.
24. If the cross examination of PW.2 is perused, he has not given treatment to the petitioner.
It is deposed by PW.2 that the IQ level of the petitioner is normal.

It is admitted by PW.2 that the GCS level of the petitioner is normal and all the external injuries are healed and the petitioner can do her day to day work to some extent and that the petitioner has not undergone surgery and there is no necessity of her taking further treatment and that the petitioner has no behavioral problem.
It is admitted by PW.2 that the petitioner can walk without any support and he has not verified any document for the further treatment taken by the petitioner.
25. As observed supra, PW.2 has assessed the Neuropsychological disability of the petitioner at 10%.
26. If the evidence of PW.1 is perused, she has given rational answer to all the questions posed to her without any hindrance even for a while.
Further it is the petitioner herself has represented the case without her being represented through guardian.

Now at this juncture it would be relevant to refer here the judgment rendered in MFA No.9065/2019 c/w MFA No.3748/2019 between Raghugowda Vs. The Mangaing Director, BMTC, wherein, in the similar set of facts the doctor has reported that petitioner has sustained 50% disability but the court while observing that the petitioner has filed Jayamma vs B.M.T.C on 4 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/34857412/
5 application on his own and as a normal person he has prosecuted the petition, he has given evidence on his own and he is a normal person with normal intellect has observed that petitioner has not suffered any disability and only with a view to get higher compensation, he has chosen to produce a false report and PW.2 being a responsible doctor has not only given a false report but also given evidence on oath based on such false report has decline to consider the percentage of disability allegedly suffered by the petitioner.

entities.text: Raghugowda Vs. The Mangaing Director, BMTC
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 27. The observation made in the aforesaid ruling is aptly applicable to the case in hand.
Hence, this court declines to consider the evidence of PW.2 and intern declines to consider the neurological disability assessed by the PW.2.

But it can be said that, when petitioner has sustained some injuries ,
because of the injuries suffered by her it may have caused some amount of loss of amenities and discomfort.
Hence, petitioner is entitled for compensation under the head loss of amenities and discomfort but not under the head loss of future income.
28. Hence, considering the nature of injuries sustained, period of treatment taken this court is of the opinion that petitioner is entitled for compensation under different heads.
29. Towards pain and sufferings, the petitioner shown to have sustained three simple injuries.

Hence taking in to consideration the nature of injuries sustained, time taken for treatment and sufferings during the treatment, it is reasonable to hold that petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.50,000/- towards pain and suffering.
30. Regarding treatment and medical expenses incurred etc, the petitioner has taken treatment at Regal Hospital, Bangalore.
To that effect she has produced medical bills for Rs.51,717/- at Ex.P9.

Hence, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under the head medical expenses to the tune of Rs. 51,717/-.
31.
It is submitted by the petitioner that at the time of accident, she was aged about 54 years and she was doing flower business and earning Rs.700/- per day.
But to prove the avocation and income, the petitioner has not produced any document.
The accident in question has occurred in the year 2024.

Hence this court considering the age of the petitioner, the year of accident and place of residence of the petitioner considers the income of the petitioner as Rs.16,500/- p.m.
32.
The petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and taken treatment for 4 days as inpatient in Regal Hospital, Bangalore.
Hence the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner which are grievous in nature it is reasonable to hold that period of 2 months as complete laid down period.
Hence petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.33,000/- towards loss of income during the laid down period .
33. From the evidence of Pw1 and as borne out by medical records, petitioner has taken treatment at Regal Hospital, Bangalore.
Further for 4 days of hospitalization requires an attendant, was traveled to hospital for treatment.
She has taken nourishment and needs further nourishment at this age and incurred other incidental expenses.

Therefore all together incidental expenses is assessed at Rs.20,000/- taking in to consideration the cost of living and value of the money during the year Jayamma vs B.M.T.C on 4 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/34857412/
6 2024.
34.

entities.text: Jayamma vs B.M.T.C on 4 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The petitioner at her age of 54 years has suffered permanent disability, hence definitely some amount of discomfort and loss of amenities and discomfort would have caused to the petitioner.
Hence he is entitled for sum of Rs.50,000/- towards loss of amenities and discomfort.

Thus the Petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
 Sl. Heads Amount  No.
 1. Towards pain and sufferings Rs. 50,000/-
 2. Medical expenses Rs. 51,717/-
 3. Loss of income during laid down Rs. 33,000/-
 period  4. Towards Conveyance, Attendant Rs. 20,000/-
 charges and nourishing food  & other incidental charges 5. Loss of discomfort and amenities Rs. 50,000/-
Total Rs
Therefore this court holds that petitioner is entitled for Rs.2,04,717/- (Rupees Two Lakh Four Thousand Seven Hundred Seventeen only).

Admittedly the respondent has paid sum of Rs.10,000/-
towards interim compensation.

Hence after deducting sum of Rs.10,000/- received by the petitioner towards interim compensation, she is entitled for sum of Rs.1,94,717/- only as compensation amount .
35.
As regarding liability is concerned, the Respondent being the RC owner cum insurer of the offending vehicle is liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.

Hence by fastening liability on the respondent this court directs the respondent to pay compensation to the petitioner along with interest at 6% per annum from the date of accident till the date of payment of entire amount.
Accordingly Issue No. 3 is answered.
36. Issue No.3: In the light of findings given on Issue No.1 & 2, my finding on this issue is as per the following final order.
ORDER The claim petition filed by the petitioner is hereby allowed in part with costs.
The petitioner is entitled to a total compensation of Rs.1,94,717/- + cost of Rs.500/- imposed vide order on IA No.II.
The petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.1,95,217/- (Rupees One Lakh Ninety Five Thousand Two Hundred Seventeen only).
A Sum of Rs.1,94,717/- shall also carry interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
Jayamma vs B.M.T.C on 4 September, 2025

Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/34857412/
7

The Respondent is liable to pay the compensation and is directed to deposit the compensation along with interest within 30 days from the date of award.
On deposit of the said amount and interest

50% of compensation payable to the petitioner shall be deposited in her name in any nationalized bank of the choice of petitioner for a period of 3 years and the remaining 50% shall be released to the petitioner through E-payment on proper identification.
Advocates' fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
(Dictated to the stenographer directly on computer, corrected and then pronounced by me in open court, on this the 4th day of September 2025.)
(ROOPASHRI) XXII Addl. SCJ & ACJM Bengaluru.
